correctness.rationale: Under total-entry-sum-one and full Frobenius normalization, each normalized hollow block has squared norm 1/(2ab); a star has squared norm (n+1)/(2n²), with its diagonal counted once. Top-right overlaps are coordinatewise minima in a and b; they do not intersect lower-left blocks even across different vertices, since simultaneous overlap would violate admissibility. This gives the three distance families in Proof §1. Hollow distances are strictly below 1/2 and star–star distances equal 1/n, so only H_(1,1)/interior-star pairs attain the printed larger diameter for n≥3; the n=2 star pair is checked separately. Strict convexity of squared distance in each argument shows that an arbitrary diametral pair must be a vertex pair. For a star in the top a rows, increasing b strictly decreases the mixed distance, then at b=n−a the resulting expression strictly increases with a, selecting a=1, i=1. Simultaneous reversal of the row and column indices gives the other minimum at i=n (ordinary matrix transpose fixes every vertex, so it is index reversal that is used in Proof §3). A nested hollow pair minimizes only if it differs by one step, since all steps have positive increments. For a crossing pair each exclusive support contributes at least 1/(4M_n), with joint equality impossible for n≥4: equality in b²≤2(b−1)b and c²≤2(c−1)c forces b=c=2, then a=d=1, whereas M_n≥(n−2)(n−1)>2. The forward difference of the cubic changes sign at b=(2n−4)/3, producing one maximizer except for two adjacent maximizers at n≡2 mod 3. The explicit n=2,3,4 comparisons and the bound M_n≥2(n−3)(n−2) for n≥5 complete the full-simplex comparison; rescaling b by n gives M_n∼4n³/27 and the stated ratio. The cutoff is at matrix order n=5, not affine dimension five. Replay RESULT.md Proof §§1–5; the exact-rational checker and its finite coverage through n=12 were inspected, not executed. This is a full-matrix metric result for the stated simplex, not a minimum distance between arbitrary points.
